blindSummary:
Trans visitors to this country face a severe risk environment. A colonial-era sodomy law (buggery, up to 10 years) remains on the books and shapes police culture; there is no legal gender recognition and no anti-discrimination protection. The defining case is a gender-nonconforming 16-year-old beaten, stabbed and shot to death by a mob at a 2013 street party after being outed — a killing police failed to investigate, now the subject of a case before a regional human-rights commission documenting the state's failure to protect trans life.

Police harassment of trans women is documented in the public-health literature, and mob justice against perceived LGBT people remains a live risk — community members report that violence against trans people (beatings, stonings) is common but rarely reported because there is no point. The main resort areas are heavily insulated bubbles where incidents are rare, but a visibly trans visitor outside them faces real outing-violence risk with indifferent police.
blindOutOfScope: The buggery law is a situational/climate factor; resort vs. non-resort risk differs sharply.
blindTangential: The buggery law (up to 10 years) is a formal exposure for visitors travelling with partners and shapes police culture.
blindSourceSummaries: Amicus brief (Feb 2024) to a regional human-rights commission in a case over the murder of a trans teenager, presented by the national trans advocacy organisation together with regional trans organisations and law-school clinics: documents systemic discrimination against LGBTQ people in this country, with transgender people particularly vulnerable to housing insecurity and educational/employment exclusion.

A foreign tribunal's response to an information request (Dec 2010) on how this country's police treat complaints by LGBT people (2007-2010): NGOs document police harassment - mostly verbal abuse but also physical abuse; the sodomy law (up to 10 years with hard labour) and 'gross indecency' between males (up to 2 years) are used to harass men perceived to be gay.

Regional inter-governmental body's report on the human-rights situation in this country (Aug 2012): comprehensive official assessment - citizen security, police killings (including May 2010), administration of justice, police impunity, and the situation of LGBT persons.
